rounds.text: Newtime Infrastructure Ltd possesses exceptional long-term top-line momentum, demonstrated by a remarkable compounded sales growth rate of 38% over the past 10 years [E13]. This fundamental revenue expansion underpins the screening engine's identification of accelerating earnings growth [E50], signaling an underlying operational turnaround that the market has yet to fully appreciate. Furthermore, the company commands a significant structural growth premium over the broader sector median sales growth of 11.6% [E57]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth has contracted by 22% [E15] alongside negative return metrics including an ROE of -15.17% [E8], and the stock currently trades low in its 52-week range at just 18% of the way up from its low [E4]. Nevertheless, the current market capitalisation of ₹ 98.7 Cr [E2] offers an accessible entry point for a platform with such proven multi-year compounding capabilities.

Newtime Infrastructure Ltd trades at a negative price-to-earnings ratio of -17.18x, which starkly contrasts with the positive sector benchmark of 18.13x [E5]. Compounded sales growth has severely deteriorated, collapsing from a 10-year rate of 38% down to just 3% over 3 years and contracting to -22% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15]. Furthermore, profitability metrics are deeply negative, with a return on equity of -15.17% and a return on assets of -8.03%, both lagging far behind respective sector benchmarks [E7, E8]. Despite this fundamental weakness, the company commands a price-to-book ratio of 2.78x against a sector benchmark of 1.42x, indicating that the valuation is significantly inflated relative to peers [E6]. Expectations are dangerously running ahead of delivery, as recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 51% [E41]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a strong 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 38% and a screening signal noting accelerating earnings growth [E13, E50].

The bear overstates the significance of the negative trailing P/E of -17.18x [E5] while ignoring the fundamental screen reason explicitly signaling that earnings growth is accelerating [E50]. The comparison to sector return benchmarks [E7, E8] overlooks the company's proven long-term capability, demonstrated by an exceptional 38% compounded sales growth rate over a 10-year period [E13]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has moderated over 3 years and the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], alongside a near-term contraction in year-over-year sales [E52]. However, the price-to-book valuation [E6] is supported by this historical top-line expansion capacity [E13] and the active acceleration in earnings [E50], which together justify the current market capitalisation of ₹ 98.7 Cr [E2] sitting near the lower end of its 52-week range [E4].

The bull's reliance on accelerating earnings [E50] to dismiss the negative trailing P/E of -17.18x [E5] collapses when confronted with a trailing twelve-month sales contraction of -22% [E15] and a year-over-year sales decline of -19% [E52]. Conceded: the company achieved a 38% compounded sales growth rate over a 10-year period [E13]. However, citing this historical long-term capability ignores the acute growth collapse witnessed in recent windows, where 3-year compounded sales growth decelerated to a meager 3% [E14]. Furthermore, the bull attempts to justify a premium price-to-book ratio of 2.78x against a sector benchmark of 1.42x [E6] using past expansion, while completely overlooking that the business delivers a destructive ROE of -15.17% and ROA of -8.03% compared to positive sector benchmarks [E7, E8]. Finally, the claim that valuation is supported by a market capitalization of ₹ 98.7 Cr [E2] near the lower end of its 52-week range [E4] ignores the reality that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 51% [E41], proving that expectations are severely running ahead of operational delivery.
